trades.name: ZS
trades.why: Bloomberg reports CrowdStrike, about seven times Zscaler's size, is in talks to buy it; the 16% pop comes off a close that was down 24% in a month, so 226 is still well under any price a founder-led board would take, and a market bounce cushions the fall-back if the talks die.
trades.wrong_if: CrowdStrike, Zscaler or Jay Chaudhry denies the talks; or Bloomberg, Reuters, the WSJ or the FT reports they have ended or stalled; or a deal is announced worth about $230 a share or less at CrowdStrike's price that day, inside the window.

trades.name: XLK/XLU
trades.why: Friday's 6.5% drop in tech against utilities was forced selling with credit calm and yields falling, and Sunday night shows the first bid across every asset in a week: a two-session relief bounce in the most-sold sector, closed before Wednesday's PCE.
trades.wrong_if: On Monday 11-23 the bounce fails in the cash session, with the Nasdaq Composite closing lower on the day; or the SEC or DOJ confirms a formal investigation of Nvidia or Nvidia says a filing will be late; or Williams or a Fed governor backs a 50 bp hike for 12-9, inside the window.
trades.stood_down: stood down by hand: the owner said to stop trying for a fill (2026-11-22, 10:23 PM CT); XLU had no overnight fills in 12 tries

trades.name: CSIQ
trades.why: A report that Canadian Solar and Recurrent hired advisers and are weighing Chapter 11 has gone a full session and a weekend with no denial, and the stock is flat at a 52-week low on a morning solar is up 5-7%: the story is its own and still running.
trades.wrong_if: Canadian Solar or Recurrent publicly denies weighing Chapter 11 or hiring restructuring advisers; or announces a Recurrent sale, asset sale or financing that pays down debt outside a court process; or Bloomberg, Reuters or the WSJ reports a buyer or rescue investor, inside the window.

trades.name: IP
trades.why: International Paper is down about 4% on 4.7 times normal volume on the market's biggest up day in years while its subpoenaed peers Packaging Corp and Smurfit Westrock are up 2-4%: the selling is IP's own (three guide cuts, negative free cash flow, an uncovered dividend, a DOJ grand-jury subpoena) and nothing dated inside the window stops it.
trades.wrong_if: International Paper announces a sale of or a buyer for its EMEA (DS Smith) business; or reaffirms or raises its Q4 EBITDA or full-year free-cash-flow guide in a filing or at an investor event; or the DOJ containerboard inquiry is reported closed or settled; or two or more covering brokers upgrade it, inside the window.
